# How Hydrogen Water May Help Calm Inflammatory Bowel Disease

Scientists found that special gases in your stomach and intestines, especially hydrogen, might help calm down the painful swelling that happens with inflammatory bowel disease. This discovery opens up new ways to help people who suffer from conditions like [Crohn's Disease](/explore-by-condition/crohn-s-disease) and [Ulcerative Colitis](/explore-by-condition/ulcerative-colitis).

## What the Research Shows

The [original research study](/study/new-insights-into-the-application-of-gastrointestinal-gases-in-inflammatory-bowel-disease-1777577956391) revealed that hydrogen gas naturally made in our bodies can act like a medicine. When hydrogen builds up in the gut, it helps reduce inflammation. This inflammation is what causes the pain, cramping, and other symptoms in people with [Inflammatory Bowel Disease](/explore-by-condition/inflammatory-bowel-disease). The research suggests that adding more hydrogen to the digestive system could be a new treatment option.

## How Hydrogen Water Delivery Works

Molecular hydrogen (H2) is a tiny gas molecule that can be delivered to your body by drinking hydrogen-rich water. Water ionizers and hydrogen water machines, like those from Echo Water™, create this special water by dissolving hydrogen gas into regular water. The study looked at how gastrointestinal gases, including hydrogen, work in the digestive system. When you drink hydrogen water, the H2 travels through your stomach and intestines, where it can help reduce harmful inflammation.

## How to Apply This Hydrogen Therapy

While this research is still new, here's how you might use hydrogen water based on what scientists know so far:

**Daily Amount:** Start with 1-2 glasses (8-16 ounces) of hydrogen water per day. Some people work up to 3-4 glasses daily.

**Best Times:** Drink hydrogen water on an empty stomach for better absorption. Try having it first thing in the morning and between meals.

**Consistency Matters:** The anti-inflammatory effects work best when hydrogen levels stay steady in your body. This means drinking hydrogen water regularly, not just once in a while.

**Track Your Response:** Keep notes about how you feel. People with digestive issues often notice changes in their symptoms over several weeks.

## What to Look For in Hydrogen Water Quality

Not all hydrogen water machines are the same. Here's what makes a quality device:

**High Hydrogen Concentration:** Look for machines that produce water with dissolved H2 levels above 1.0 ppm (parts per million). Higher concentrations mean more therapeutic hydrogen.

**ORP Levels:** Good hydrogen water should have a negative ORP (oxidation reduction potential) reading. This shows the water has antioxidant properties.

**Third-Party Testing:** Choose machines that have been tested by independent labs. This proves the hydrogen levels are real and consistent.

**Fresh Production:** Hydrogen gas escapes from water quickly. The best machines make fresh hydrogen water on demand, rather than storing it.

## Key Takeaways for Hydrogen Water Use

• **New Treatment Path**: This research from the [hydrogen general research](/blog/category/general) field shows hydrogen therapy might help people with inflammatory bowel conditions in a completely new way.

• **Natural Approach**: Your body already makes some hydrogen gas naturally. Drinking hydrogen water just adds more of this helpful molecule to support your digestive system.

• **Start Slowly**: If you have IBD or other digestive problems, begin with small amounts of hydrogen water and see how your body responds before increasing.

• **Combine with Medical Care**: Hydrogen water should add to your current treatment plan, not replace medicines your doctor has prescribed for inflammatory conditions.

The research on gastrointestinal gases and hydrogen therapy is growing fast. Scientists are learning more about how these tiny molecules can help with inflammation throughout the body. You can explore more studies in our [hydrogen research database](/proxy/) to stay updated on the latest findings.

Remember that inflammatory bowel disease affects everyone differently. What works for one person may not work the same way for another. The key is finding the right combination of treatments that help you feel better.

**Disclaimer:** Consult your healthcare provider before starting any new health regimen, especially if you have inflammatory bowel disease or other digestive conditions.
